agents.result: I renamed `send_file`'s `download_name` parameter to `filename` in the signature, docstring and body of `src/flask/helpers.py`, and all 491 tests pass. No caller in the repo passed the old keyword, so nothing else changed. Werkzeug's own `download_name` argument stays as is, and I left the version-history notes and `CHANGES.rst` alone. When the other engineer's `send_text` merges, it must call `send_file(..., filename=name)`, because `download_name=` will now raise a `TypeError`.

I added `send_text(text, name)` to the end of `src/flask/helpers.py` and exported it from `src/flask/__init__.py`, and the test suite passes (491 passed, 3 skipped), though I couldn't do a quick manual check of the response because that command needed approval; it passes `name` to `send_file` by position rather than as `download_name=` so it keeps working after the other engineer renames that parameter to `filename`.

+def send_text(text: str, name: str) -> Response:
+    """Send a string to the client as a downloadable plain text file.
+
+    :param text: The text to send. It is encoded as UTF-8.
+    :param name: The file name the browser will save the file as.
+    """
+    # The name is passed positionally so this call does not depend on
+    # the keyword name of send_file's download name parameter.
+    return send_file(io.BytesIO(text.encode("utf-8")), "text/plain", True, name)
